text:
Situation: As of 2026-10-21, labetalol hydrochloride is not on FDA's drug shortage list. Corvale East holds 301 tablets of the 100 mg presentation with 11.4 tablets used per day, providing 26.3 days on hand. Corvale General holds 297 tablets with 13.8 tablets used per day, providing 21.6 days on hand.

Why (FDA record): The current product label names Heritage Pharma Labs Inc. d/b/a Avet Pharmaceuticals Labs Inc. (FEI 3005139373) as the registered manufacturing plant. FDA inspection records for that plant show multiple VAI classifications from 2009 through 2018, with the most recent inspection ending 2018-02-06 resulting in a VAI classification, and a NAI classification on 2023-09-19.

Our position: Current inventory provides approximately three weeks of supply at both campuses. No FDA shortage listing exists to trigger allocation protocols. Alternative manufacturers are available for purchase but their labels do not identify verifiable manufacturing plants.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to initiate purchase from Advagen Pharma Ltd. as the top-ranked option; requires P&T committee approval for formulary addition.
2. Buyer to qualify Biocon Pharma Inc. as secondary source; requires P&T committee approval for formulary addition.
3. Buyer to qualify BluePoint Laboratories as tertiary source; requires P&T committee approval for formulary addition.
4. Buyer to monitor daily usage and update days-on-hand projections weekly; requires pharmacy director approval.
5. Buyer to request plant identification from all alternative suppliers before first order; requires quality assurance approval.

Not recommended: Delaying procurement until inventory falls below 14 days. Switching products without P&T committee review. Assuming supply continuity based solely on absence from FDA shortage list.
